claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation

  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help determine your eligibility, I need to start with some basic information about your child(ren).

**What is your child's age?** (Or if you have multiple children, please tell me about each one)

This will help me understand which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one son, Alex, who is 18 years old.

Since Alex is between 16 and 19, I need to check some additional details about his education or training status.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or an approved training course?**

This is important because young people aged 16-19 can qualify for Child Benefit if they're in qualifying education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is in full-time education studying for A-levels, which is a qualifying educational course. Let me navigate through the decision tree to check the next steps.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me proceed based on Alex's current education status:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! I can see that A-levels are on the list of approved qualifications. Let me check a couple more details to ensure Alex meets all the requirements:

**A few quick questions to confirm:**

1. **Is Alex studying A-levels at least 12 hours per week with supervised study time?** (This is typically the case at sixth form colleges, but I want to confirm)

2. **Is Alex working full-time while studying, or is he studying full-time?** (Child Benefit doesn't apply if a young person is working full-time, even if they're also studying)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
1. Yes, he's at sixth form full-time, so definitely more than 12 hours a week of supervised study.

2. No, he's not working at all - he's just focusing on his studies.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Based on the information you've provided, let me navigate through the remaining checks to confirm Alex's eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Since Alex isn't working at all, this requirement is definitely met. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: **Is Alex receiving Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in his own right?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: **Is Alex in an apprenticeship program?** If so, which type and in which country (England, Scotland, or Wales)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - he's just doing his A-levels at sixth form.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. This is important for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this covers most UK residents)

2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**

3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (and I'd need to know your employment/study situation)

4. **You are a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

5. **Or does something else apply to your situation?**

For most people in the UK, option 1 (normally living in the UK) applies. Which one fits your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I live here with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That confirms you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex. This means:

**Do any of the following apply?**

1. **You live with Alex** (sounds like this is the case based on what you've said)

2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** even if you don't live with him (e.g., paying for food, clothes, housing, pocket money)

3. **You pay maintenance** towards Alex's care under a court order or agreement

Based on what you've already told me, it sounds like option 1 applies - you live with Alex. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else indicated they might claim for him?**

This could include:
- Alex's other parent
- A grandparent
- Another carer or relative

Or is it just you who would be claiming?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Where is Alex currently living?**

- At home with you (normal living situation)
- In hospital
- In care (children's home, residential school, etc.)
- In a fostering arrangement

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's at home with me - just a normal living situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! One final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you fully supporting Alex at home without the council paying for his housing or upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - the council isn't paying anything. I'm supporting him myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me navigate to the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me provide you with the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Good News! You are **ELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit

---

### Summary for Alex:

✅ **You can claim Child Benefit for your son Alex**

Alex meets all the eligibility criteria because:
- He is 18 years old and in full-time approved education (A-levels)
- He studies more than 12 hours per week with supervised study
- He is not working full-time
- He is not receiving benefits in his own right
- He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- You live in the UK and are responsible for him by living with him
- No one else is claiming for him
- The council is not paying towards his accommodation
- He is living at home with you in a normal living situation

---

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for both yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, there may be a tax charge on your Child Benefit
5. **Payments** will be made every 4 weeks to your bank account

### Important Reminders:

⏰ **Alex's eligibility will continue** as long as he remains in full-time approved education or training. However, once he turns 20 or leaves full-time education (whichever comes first), his eligibility will end unless other qualifying circumstances apply.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the claim process?

You normally live in the UK, are responsible for Alex by living with him, are the only person claiming for him, the council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance, and he is living in a normal home situation. Alex therefore meets all the criteria for Child Benefit eligibility.
